newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Mercedes says 8-month sales up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mercedes says 8-month sales up 10 pct.

text.p: German car-maker Mercedes-Benz AG said on Monday that its vehicle sales during the first eight months of 1996 rose about 10 percent and accelerated during the last few months.

Mercedes chief executive Helmut Werner said the carmaker, a unit of industrial group Daimler-Benz AG, sold 423,000 vehicles during the period from January to August. In the first half of the year, Werner said Mercedes sales rose about seven percent.
Sales of Mercedes passenger cars in Germany from January to August also surged 15 percent over year-ago levels, he said.
Werner, speaking at a news conference to introduce the new Mercedes V-class mini-van, said he expected the positive developments at Mercedes to continue in the year's second half.
Werner said he saw essentially little change in the truck market but said that positive response to the new "Actros" heavy truck was expected to provide impetus for the European market.
Mercedes said its transport vehicle sales in Europe through the end of August rose 26 percent to 81,000 vehicles.

The new mini-van, based on the Mercedes transporter Vito, will be built at the group's Spanish plant in Vitoria. Werner said he expected annual production of the new vehicle at about 16,000 units, a level he said was very conservative.
Mercedes has invested about one billion marks into the development of the two vehicles and the plant, which will have annual production of about 80,000 units.

The new V-class vehicle, to be on sale starting Friday, is the last new model that Mercedes will introduce in 1996. Mercedes is planning for 1997 to introduce a new couple, four-wheel drive vehicle and the new A-class compact. -- Frankfurt newsroom +49 69 756524
